boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along downtown and riverfront corridors within Loras College’s practical off-campus orbit, each paired with one documented reason to go.

cards.title: Find the Library Rotunda
cards.subtitle: West 11th Street at Bluff Street
cards.notes: Enter from West 11th Street and look up inside the historic rotunda, where a domed light well, Corinthian columns, and original finishes define the space.
cards.short_summary: A working public library inside a landmark Classical Revival building.
cards.evidence_claim: The city identifies Carnegie-Stout Public Library at 360 W. 11th St. and documents its central rotunda, Corinthian columns, marble flooring, and white-oak woodwork.
cards.access_notes: Public library hours and holiday closures can change; confirm the current schedule on the library website before entering.

cards.title: See the Restored Steeple Campus
cards.subtitle: East 15th Street beside the Central Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Approach from East 15th Street for a clear exterior view, then contact Steeple Square directly if you want to arrange a tour of the event-center campus.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable community campus anchored by a historic church steeple.
cards.evidence_claim: Steeple Square lists its campus at 101 East 15th Street and provides direct contacts for tours, volunteer opportunities, programs, and events.
cards.access_notes: Interior access is program- or arrangement-dependent; use the official tour contact before planning to enter.

cards.title: Enter Through Dupaco Alley
cards.subtitle: 10th Street in the Historic Millwork District
cards.notes: Use the museum’s specified Dupaco Alley entrance on 10th Street, then check the current exhibition list before choosing what to see inside.
cards.short_summary: A local art stop with an unusually specific alley-side entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dubuque Museum of Art says its current space is in the Millwork District and directs visitors to enter via Dupaco Alley on 10th Street between Jackson and Washington.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists Wednesday-Sunday visitor hours, with later Thursday hours; verify closures and exhibitions before visiting.

cards.title: Catch a Community Production
cards.subtitle: West 8th Street at Iowa Street
cards.notes: Check the production calendar before walking down West 8th Street; the historic venue presents community-focused theatre, dance, and performing-arts programs.
cards.short_summary: A nineteenth-century theater still operating as a nonprofit performance venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grand Opera House documents that it has served Dubuque since 1890 and now operates as the city’s largest nonprofit theatre.
cards.access_notes: Entry generally depends on a scheduled performance or program; consult the official calendar and ticket details.

cards.title: Pause at the Gazebo
cards.subtitle: Locust Street between West 6th and West 7th streets
cards.notes: Walk in from Locust Street and use the gazebo as your visual landmark; benches, picnic tables, vegetation, and a city time capsule fill the block.
cards.short_summary: A full downtown park block centered on a highly photographable gazebo.
cards.evidence_claim: The city locates Washington Park at 700 Locust Street and lists its gazebo, planted areas, time capsule, benches, picnic tables, and water fountains.
cards.access_notes: The city lists seasonal park hours from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.; amenities may be unavailable outside the stated park season.

cards.title: Frame the Clock from Main Street
cards.subtitle: Main Street at Town Clock Plaza
cards.notes: Stand back along Main Street to fit the elevated clock and its four-column pedestal into one frame, then compare the structure with nearby storefront scale.
cards.short_summary: A 110-foot downtown landmark raised above its pedestrian plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: The city says the Town Clock stands in Town Clock Plaza on Main Street, was moved there in 1971, and reaches approximately 110 feet when assembled.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from Town Clock Plaza; nearby festivals or street activity can temporarily affect access.

cards.title: Use the Locust Street Entrance
cards.subtitle: Main Street between West 4th and West 5th streets
cards.notes: When attending an event, approach the Main Street venue from its signed Locust Street entrance between Fourth and Fifth streets and review the bag policy first.
cards.short_summary: A downtown civic and entertainment complex spanning an arena and historic theater.
cards.evidence_claim: Five Flags Center lists its address as 405 Main Street and specifies that its visitor entrance is on Locust Street between Fourth and Fifth streets.
cards.access_notes: Building entry is event-dependent; check the official schedule, ticket requirements, entrance details, and current bag policy.

cards.title: Ride Above Fourth Street
cards.subtitle: West 4th Street at Bluff Street
cards.notes: Start at Fourth and Bluff for the lower station, bring cash for the fare, and ride the 296-foot funicular toward Fenelon Place for the elevated view.
cards.short_summary: A compact seasonal funicular climbing directly from downtown to the bluff.
cards.evidence_claim: The operator describes the Fenelon Place Elevator as a 296-foot funicular rising 189 feet from Fourth Street to Fenelon Place and directs GPS users to Fourth and Bluff streets.
cards.access_notes: The operator lists seasonal daily service from April 1 through November 30, excluding Thanksgiving, and says payment is cash only.

cards.title: Follow Third Street to the River
cards.subtitle: East 3rd Street in the Port of Dubuque
cards.notes: Take the Third Street bridge toward the Port and follow the museum’s alternate directions if rail traffic blocks the more common Fifth Street approach.
cards.short_summary: A combined aquarium, river-history museum, and science center on the waterfront.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum locates its campus at 350 East 3rd Street in the Port of Dubuque and describes it as part museum, part aquarium, and part science center.
cards.source_title: Maps & Directions | National Mississippi River Museum & Aquarium
cards.access_notes: Admission is ticketed; verify current hours and use the museum’s alternate route when train traffic obstructs the Fifth Street crossing.

cards.title: Study the Stone-to-Brick Tower
cards.subtitle: Commercial Street at the Mississippi River
cards.notes: Approach from Commercial Street and study the exterior transition from seven stone stories to three brick stories; do not attempt to enter the structure.
cards.short_summary: A 120-foot industrial landmark built for nineteenth-century lead-shot production.
cards.evidence_claim: The city locates the Shot Tower at Commercial Street and the Mississippi River and documents its seven stone stories, three brick stories, and 120-foot height.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior landmark stop; the city page does not advertise public interior access.
